case_title.quote: R. SHAJI v. STATE OF KERALA

number_of_accused.quote: The trial however, could be conducted only against two persons, i.e. the appellant (A-1) and Vinu (A-2)

accused_gender.quote: he would chop him up into pieces
accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to as male.

accused_age.reason: No age of the appellant is given in the judgment.

accused_occupation.quote: the appellant at the relevant time had been working as the Deputy Superintendent of Police at Malappuram

previous_criminal_record.reason: No criminal record mentioned for the appellant.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Related (relative); victim was driver of accused's wife and had an illicit relationship with her
accused_victim_relationship.quote: using a vehicle which was driven by Praveen (deceased). He was also related to the appellant.
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused was not the victim's spouse; victim was a related driver of his wife.

offence_category.quote: convicted under Section 302 read with Section 120-B

statutory_provisions.quote: Section 302 read with Section 120-B... Section 201... Section 364 read with Section 120-B
statutory_provisions.reason: All sections listed are in the judgment.

weapon.quote: The chopper (M.0.4), alleged to have been used in the said crime

evidence_type.quote: The prosecution case was based on circumstantial evidence.

confession.correct_value: No confession; disclosure statements under s.27 Evidence Act led to recoveries
confession.quote: the appellant made a disclosure statement to the effect that Praveen's body was mutilated using the chopper
confession.reason: No confession, but disclosure statements were made and relied upon.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Motive, use of van, dismemberment of body, conspiracy; the court did not formally list aggravating circumstances
aggravating_circumstances.quote: The motive as explained hereinabove stood proved.
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Items are proof circumstances, not framed as aggravating by the court.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: Convicted under ss.302/120-B (life, fine Rs.1 lakh), 201/120-B (3 years) and 364/120-B (7 years RI)
trial_court_outcome.quote: awarded a sentence of life imprisonment and a fine of Rs. one lakh
trial_court_outcome.reason: Omits other convictions and sentences and fine.

high_court_outcome.quote: Criminal Appeal No. 86 of 2006, which was dismissed by the High Court
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court did decide, dismissing the appeal; not 'Not applicable'.

final_outcome.quote: we do not find any merit in the appeal and the same is dismissed

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Murder with criminal conspiracy (s.302/120-B), concealment of evidence (s.201/120-B), kidnapping/abduction (s.364/120-B)
offence_finally_established.quote: convicted under Section 201 read with Section 120-B IPC... Section 364 read with Section 120-B IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Criminal trespass and disappearance of a person are not the offences; s.364 is kidnapping for murder.

imprisonment_type.quote: awarded a sentence of life imprisonment

imprisonment_years.reason: Life term, no years for main sentence; null acceptable.

fine_rs.correct_value: Rs. 1,00,000 for s.302/120-B (plus Rs.2,000 and Rs.5,000 for other counts)
fine_rs.quote: a fine of Rs. one lakh, in default of which, he would undergo SI for a period of one year
fine_rs.reason: A fine was imposed; null is wrong.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts without outcome-revealing language; avoid 'was involved in the murder' and conspiracy as established
neutral_facts.quote: The motive as explained hereinabove stood proved.
neutral_facts.reason: Largely accurate but asserts guilt (involved in murder, conspiracy), revealing outcome.

offence_severity.correct_value: s.302 IPC: death or life imprisonment (and fine)
offence_severity.reason: Minimum for s.302 is life, not death; statutory range not discussed in judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: Praveen died in the intervening night between 15/16.2.2005.

physical_harm.quote: dismemberment of the parts of the body was possible by using a weapon like the chopper

number_of_offences.correct_value: Convicted of three sets of offences: s.302/120-B, s.201/120-B, s.364/120-B
number_of_offences.quote: Both the accused were also convicted under Section 201 read with Section 120-B IPC... Section 364
number_of_offences.reason: 'Five offences charged, two upheld' is not supported; all three convictions were upheld.

premeditation_planning.quote: together they had hatched a conspiracy to eliminate Praveen (deceased)

motive.quote: he may well have been unable to tolerate the intimacy that the deceased had developed with his wife

key_evidence_accepted.quote: recovery of the said chopper at the behest of the appellant cannot be doubted

witness_credibility.correct_value: Court held evidence weighed not counted; PW.12 not disbelieved in toto; PW.8, PW.11 argument rejected; PW.11 turned hostile
witness_credibility.quote: we do not find any cogent reason to dis-believe the testimony of Shanavas (PW.12) in toto
witness_credibility.reason: Broadly right but generalises; some witnesses hostile and not fully credited.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Appellant posted a letter in the victim's name to mislead the family; led police to chopper, skull and van
post_offence_conduct.quote: This letter seems to have been written to misdirect/mislead the deceased's family.
post_offence_conduct.reason: Misses real post-offence conduct and confuses conviction with conduct.

trial_duration.correct_value: Trial court 3.1.2006; HC 10.12.2009; SC judgment 4 February 2013
trial_duration.reason: SC decision date given as 24.2.2013 is wrong (24.2.2005 is arrest date).

legal_representation.quote: Dr. S. Gopakumaran Nair, T.G. Naray~nan Nair, K.N. Madhusoodhanan for ttie Appellant.

investigation_status.quote: a charge sheet was filed against five persons, including the appellant

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Alleged non-exhibiting of s.164 statements and no TI parade; court found no vitiation
procedural_irregularity.quote: such documents, if the same were in fact, a part of the record, were not marked
procedural_irregularity.reason: Court noted unmarked s.164 statements though it rejected the objection.

appeal_history.quote: Criminal Appeal No. 86 of 2006, which was dismissed by the High Court

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State argued circumstances pointed only to appellant's guilt, DNA identified body parts, witnesses trustworthy, TI parade a formality
prosecution_argument.quote: the various circumstances that stood proved, pointed only towards the guilt of the appellant
prosecution_argument.reason: Broadly consistent but omits main submissions.

defence_argument.correct_value: Also incomplete chain, fleeting identification by witnesses, identification of body, non-examination of Aji etc.
defence_argument.quote: The chain of circumstances is not complete.
defence_argument.reason: Lists main grounds but omits others.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the prosecution must establish its case beyond reasonable doubt

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: List includes cases cited, but 'Makhhan' is misspelt (Malkhan Singh)
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Ma/khan Singh & Ors. v. State of MP. AIR 2003 SC 2669
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Cases are cited in the judgment but the list is incomplete and has a name error.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Supreme Court gave no sentencing rationale; it addressed guilt only.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Fine with default imprisonment; sentences for 201/120-B (3 yrs) and 364/120-B (7 yrs RI) to run concurrently
other_sentence_order.quote: All the sentences were directed to run concurrently.
other_sentence_order.reason: Other sentences and concurrency order exist.
